test.title: Part 1–4: Cambridge IELTS 19 Academic Listening Test 1

items.quote: Altogether the park covers 170 acres, that's 69 hectares.
items.prompt: Area: ____ hectares

explanation.en: The park covers 69 hectares; 170 is the area in acres, so the units decide the answer.
explanation.kk: Аумағы — 69 гектар; 170 акрға қатысты, сондықтан өлшем бірлігін ажырату қажет.
explanation.ru: Площадь — 69 гектаров; 170 относится к акрам, поэтому важно различать единицы.

items.quote: There are also several smaller ones, ponds and a stream that flows through the park.
items.prompt: Wetland: lakes, ponds and a ____

explanation.en: A stream is listed after the lakes and ponds; keep the singular form after “a”.
explanation.kk: Көлдер мен тоғандардан кейін stream аталады; «a» сөзінен кейін жекеше түрі керек.
explanation.ru: После озёр и прудов назван ручей, stream; после «a» нужна форма единственного числа.

items.quote: They also collect and analyse data about the things they see.
items.prompt: Science: Children look at ____ about plants, etc.

explanation.en: Children collect and analyse data about what they see; plants and insects are the subject of the data.
explanation.kk: Балалар data жинап, талдайды; өсімдік пен жәндік — сол деректің тақырыбы.
explanation.ru: Дети собирают и анализируют данные, data; растения и насекомые — предмет этих данных.

items.quote: The park is a great environment to learn and practise reading a map and using a compass to navigate around the park.
items.prompt: Geography: includes learning to use a ____ and compass

explanation.en: Geography includes reading a map and using a compass; “compass” is already supplied after the gap.
explanation.kk: Географияда map оқып, компас қолдануды үйренеді; compass бос орыннан кейін берілген.
explanation.ru: На географии учатся читать карту, map, и пользоваться компасом; compass уже дан после пропуска.

items.quote: That focuses on your visitors, I would imagine.
items.prompt: Leisure and tourism: mostly concentrates on the park’s ____

explanation.en: John identifies visitors as the focus of leisure and tourism, and Sally confirms it.
explanation.kk: Джон туризм тақырыбы ретінде visitors атайды, Салли оны растайды.
explanation.ru: Джон называет посетителей, visitors, темой туризма, и Салли подтверждает это.

items.quote: And another subject we cover is music: here the children experiment with natural materials to create sounds and explore rhythm and tempo.
items.prompt: Music: Children make ____ with natural materials, and experiment with rhythm and speed.

explanation.en: Children create sounds with natural materials; rhythm and tempo describe what they explore afterwards.
explanation.kk: Балалар табиғи материалмен sounds жасайды; ырғақ пен қарқын кейін зерттеледі.
explanation.ru: Дети создают звуки, sounds, из природных материалов; ритм и темп изучают затем.

groups.title: Hinchingbrooke Country Park — the park and educational visits
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: I would imagine they get a sense of freedom that might not be a normal part of their lives.
items.prompt: They give children a feeling of ____ that they may not have elsewhere.

explanation.en: John says outdoor learning gives children a sense of freedom, paraphrased as a “feeling” in the notes.
explanation.kk: Джон freedom сезімі туралы айтады; sense of тіркесі жазбадағы feeling сөзіне сәйкес.
explanation.ru: Джон говорит о чувстве свободы, freedom; sense of соответствует feeling в заметках.

items.quote: And very often the children discover that they can do things they didn't know they could do, and they develop new skills.
items.prompt: Children learn new ____ and gain self-confidence.

explanation.en: Sally links developing new skills to greater self-confidence; the gap asks what children learn.
explanation.kk: Салли жаңа skills пен сенімділікті байланыстырады; бос орын балалар үйренетін нәрсені сұрайды.
explanation.ru: Салли связывает новые навыки, skills, с уверенностью; в пропуске нужно то, чему дети учатся.

items.quote: If there are over 30, it costs £4.95 for each child who attends on the day.
items.prompt: Cost per child: £____

explanation.en: For a group of over 30, each attending child costs £4.95; 30–40 is the group size, not the price.
explanation.kk: 30-дан көп бала болса, әр балаға £4.95 төленеді; 30–40 — баға емес, бала саны.
explanation.ru: При группе более 30 детей цена за ребёнка — £4.95; 30–40 — число детей, а не цена.

items.quote: There's no charge for leaders and other adults — as many as you want to bring.
items.prompt: Adults, such as ____, free

explanation.en: There is no charge for leaders and other adults; use the plural “leaders” as spoken.
explanation.kk: Leaders және басқа ересектер тегін кіреді; көпше түрін сақтаңыз.
explanation.ru: Для руководителей, leaders, и других взрослых вход бесплатный; сохраните множественное число.

groups.title: Hinchingbrooke Country Park — benefits and practical issues
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A teaching assistant calls a country park about an educational visit.

transcript.text: Good morning.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Hinchingbrooke Country Park, Sally speaking.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: I'm one of the rangers.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Oh hello.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: My name's John Chapman, and I'm a teaching assistant at a local primary school.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I've been asked to arrange a visit to the park for two of our classes.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: What would you like to know?
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Well, I'm new to this area, so perhaps you could tell me something about the park first, please.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Of course.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Altogether the park covers 170 acres, that's 69 hectares.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: There are three main types of habitat: wetland, grassland and woodland.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: The woods are well established and varied, with an oak plantation, and other areas of mixed species.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: The wetland is quite varied, too.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: The original farmland was dug up around 40 years ago to extract gravel.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Once this work was completed, the gravel pits filled with water, forming the two large lakes.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: There are also several smaller ones, ponds and a stream that flows through the park.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: OK, so I suppose with these different habitats there's quite a variety of wildlife.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: There certainly is — a lot of different species of birds and insects, and also animals like deer and rabbits.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: And I understand you organise educational visits for school parties.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: That's right.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: We can organise a wide range of activities and adapt them to suit all ages.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Can you give me some examples of the activities?
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Well, one focus is on science, where we help children to discover and study plants, trees and insects.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: They also collect and analyse data about the things they see.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Uhuh.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Another focus is on geography.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: The park is a great environment to learn and practise reading a map and using a compass to navigate around the park.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Do you do anything connected with history?
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Yes, we do.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: For instance, the children can explore how the use of the land has changed over time.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Then there's leisure and tourism.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: That focuses on your visitors, I would imagine.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Yes, mostly.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: The children find out about them, their requirements, the problems they may cause and how we manage these.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: And another subject we cover is music: here the children experiment with natural materials to create sounds and explore rhythm and tempo.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: That must be fun!
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Most children really enjoy it.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: And of course, all the activities are educational, too.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Learning outside the classroom encourages children to be creative, and to explore and discover for themselves.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: I would imagine they get a sense of freedom that might not be a normal part of their lives.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: That's right.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: And very often the children discover that they can do things they didn't know they could do, and they develop new skills.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: This gives them greater self-confidence.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: It sounds great.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: So, what about the practical side of it?
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: How much does it cost for a full-day visit?
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: We would expect to bring between 30 and 40 children.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: If there are over 30, it costs £4.95 for each child who attends on the day.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: We invoice you afterwards, so you don't pay for children who can't come because of sickness, for example.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: There's no charge for leaders and other adults — as many as you want to bring.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: That sounds very fair.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: Well, thanks for all the information.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: I'll need to discuss it with my colleagues, and I hope to get back to you soon to make a booking.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

transcript.text: We'll look forward to hearing from you.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: SALLY

transcript.text: Goodbye, and thank you.
transcript.speaker: JOHN

items.quote: The theme park trip had to be cancelled, but we all had a great time on the final boat trip down the river — that was the real highlight.
items.prompt: During the visit to Malatte, in France, members especially enjoyed

options.text: going to a theme park.
experiencing a river trip.
visiting a cheese factory.

explanation.en: The river trip was the highlight; the theme park was cancelled and the cheese visit was not the highlight.
explanation.kk: Өзендегі сапар ең жақсы оқиға болды; паркке бару тоқтатылды, ірімшік негізгі әсер ретінде аталмады.
explanation.ru: Поездка по реке была главным событием; парк отменили, сыр не назван главным впечатлением.

items.quote: We've been discussing what to do here and we've decided to plant a poplar tree in the museum gardens.
items.prompt: What will happen in Stanthorpe to mark the 25th anniversary of the Twinning Association?

options.text: A tree will be planted.
A garden seat will be bought.
A footbridge will be built.

explanation.en: Stanthorpe will plant a tree; the bridge is in Malatte and the seat was rejected.
explanation.kk: Станторпта ағаш отырғызылады; көпір Малаттеде салынады, орындық ұсынысы қабылданбады.
explanation.ru: В Стэнторпе посадят дерево; мост строят в Малатте, скамейку отклонили.

items.quote: Our pancake evening was well attended and made record profits.
items.prompt: Which event raised most funds this year?

options.text: the film show
the pancake evening
the cookery demonstration

explanation.en: The pancake evening made record profits; the cookery demonstration was only nearly as successful.
explanation.kk: Құймақ кеші рекордтық табыс әкелді; аспаздық көрсетілім соған жақын болды.
explanation.ru: Блинный вечер принёс рекордную прибыль; кулинарный показ был лишь почти столь успешным.

items.quote: Don't try to do too much that first evening as they'll be tired, so have dinner in the house or garden rather than eating out.
items.prompt: For the first evening with the French visitors host families are advised to

options.text: take them for a walk round the town.
go to a local restaurant.
have a meal at home.

explanation.en: Visitors will be tired, so dinner should be at home; the stroll is suggested for the next morning.
explanation.kk: Қонақтар шаршайды, сондықтан үйде тамақтану ұсынылады; серуен келесі таңға қатысты.
explanation.ru: Гости устанут, поэтому советуют ужинать дома; прогулка относится к следующему утру.

items.quote: On Saturday evening, we'll all meet up at the football club, where once again we'll have Toby Sharp and his band performing English and Scottish country songs.
items.prompt: On Saturday evening there will be the chance to

options.text: listen to a concert.
watch a match.
take part in a competition.

explanation.en: The band will perform songs; the football club is the venue and the quiz was last year.
explanation.kk: Топ ән орындайды; футбол клубы — концерт орны, викторина өткен жылы болды.
explanation.ru: Группа исполнит песни; футбольный клуб — место концерта, викторина была в прошлом году.

groups.title: Stanthorpe Twinning Association
groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: They're built round a courtyard, and the shop's in the far corner on the left.
items.prompt: Farm shop

explanation.en: The shop is in the far left corner of the old stables, G; the café is on the right.
explanation.kk: Дүкен ескі атқораның алыс сол жақ бұрышында, G; оң жақта кафе бар.
explanation.ru: Магазин в дальнем левом углу старых конюшен, G; справа находится кафе.

items.quote: This is on the far side of the house from the car park.
items.prompt: Disabled entry

explanation.en: The entry is on the side opposite the car park, C, rather than the west-side doorway E.
explanation.kk: Кіреберіс үйдің автотұраққа қарама-қарсы жағында, C; батыстағы E емес.
explanation.ru: Вход расположен на стороне дома, противоположной парковке, C; не у западной двери E.

items.quote: That's at the northern end of the larger lake, in a bend on the path that leads to the lake.
items.prompt: Adventure playground

explanation.en: The playground is at the path bend at the north end of the larger lake, B.
explanation.kk: Алаң үлкен көлдің солтүстік шетіндегі жол иінінде, B.
explanation.ru: Площадка на изгибе дорожки у северного конца большого озера, B.

items.quote: They're to the north-east of the house, quite near the smaller lake.
items.prompt: Kitchen gardens

explanation.en: The walled rectangular area northeast of the house is D.
explanation.kk: Үйдің солтүстік-шығысындағы қабырғалы тікбұрышты жер — D.
explanation.ru: Прямоугольный участок со стеной к северо-востоку от дома — D.

items.quote: Go up there with the woods on your left and the temple is right at the end.
items.prompt: The Temple of the Four Winds

explanation.en: From the car park, pass west of the house and turn right at the fork; the path ends at A.
explanation.kk: Автотұрақтан үйдің батысымен жүріп, айырықта оңға бұрылады; жол соңы — A.
explanation.ru: От парковки идут западнее дома, затем направо на развилке; конец тропы — A.

groups.title: Farley House

options.text: End of the northern path beside woods
Bend near the northern end of the large lake
North side of the house
Walled rectangular area northeast of the house
West side of the house near the large lake
End of the path east of the house
Far left corner of the old stables
Right side of the old stables near their entrance

groups.instruction: Label the map below. Write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 16–20.

parts.context: A Twinning Association member describes recent events and a visit to Farley House.

transcript.text: It's great to see so many members of the Twinning Association here tonight.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Since the twinning link between our two towns, Stanthorpe here in England and Malatte in France, was established, the relationship between the towns has gone from strength to strength.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Last month, 25 members of the association from Stanthorpe spent a weekend in Malatte.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Our hosts had arranged a great programme.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: We learned how cheese is produced in the region and had the chance to taste the products.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The theme park trip had to be cancelled, but we all had a great time on the final boat trip down the river — that was the real highlight.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This is a special year for the Association because it's 25 years since we were founded.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In Malatte, they're planning to mark this by building a footbridge in the municipal park.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: We've been discussing what to do here and we've decided to plant a poplar tree in the museum gardens.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: We considered buying a garden seat to put there, but the authorities weren't happy with that idea.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In terms of fundraising to support our activities, we've done very well.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Our pancake evening was well attended and made record profits.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: And everyone enjoyed the demonstration of French cookery, which was nearly as successful.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Numbers for our film show were limited because of the venue so we're looking for somewhere bigger next year.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: We're looking forward to welcoming our French visitors here next week, and I know that many of you here will be hosting individuals or families.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The coach from France will arrive at 5 pm on Friday.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Don't try to do too much that first evening as they'll be tired, so have dinner in the house or garden rather than eating out.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The weather looks as if it'll be OK so you might like to plan a barbecue.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Then the next morning's market day in town, and that's always a good place to stroll round.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: On Saturday evening, we'll all meet up at the football club, where once again we'll have Toby Sharp and his band performing English and Scottish country songs.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Toby will already be well known to many of you as last year he organised our special quiz night and presented the prizes.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Now on Sunday, we'll be taking our visitors to Farley House.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: You may not all be familiar with it, so here's a map to help you.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: You can see the car park at the bottom of the map.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There's an excellent farm shop in the grounds where our visitors can buy local produce — it's in the old stables, which is the first building you come to.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They're built round a courtyard, and the shop's in the far corner on the left.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There's also a small café on the right as you go in.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: I know that one or two of our visitors may not be all that mobile.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The main entrance to the house has a lot of steps so you might want to use the disabled entry.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This is on the far side of the house from the car park.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Children will probably be most interested in the adventure playground.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: That's at the northern end of the larger lake, in a bend on the path that leads to the lake.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There's lots for children to do there.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There are a number of lovely gardens near the house.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The kitchen gardens are rectangular and surrounded by a wall.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They're to the north-east of the house, quite near the smaller lake.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They're still in use and have a great collection of fruit and vegetables.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The Temple of the Four Winds is a bit more of a walk — but it's worth it.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Take the path from the car park and go past the western sides of the stables and the house.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Then when the path forks, take the right-hand path.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Go up there with the woods on your left and the temple is right at the end.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There are great views over the whole area.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: OK, so that's .
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

items.quote: Yeah, I'd used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce.
items.prompt: Which TWO things did Colin find most satisfying about his bread reuse project?

options.text: receiving support from local restaurants
finding a good way to prevent waste
overcoming problems in a basic process
experimenting with designs and colours
learning how to apply 3-D printing

explanation.en: He enjoyed patterns and colours and preventing waste. The process was straightforward, 3-D printing was familiar, and restaurant support was only hoped for.
explanation.kk: Ол өрнек пен түстерге және қалдықты азайтуға риза. Үдеріс оңай, 3-D басып шығару таныс, мейрамханалар әлі жауап бермеген.
explanation.ru: Он доволен узорами и цветами и предотвращением отходов. Процесс был простым, 3-D печать знакома, рестораны ещё не ответили.

items.quote: But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies.
items.prompt: Which TWO ways do the students agree that touch-sensitive sensors for food labels could be developed in future?

options.text: for use on medical products
to show that food is no longer fit to eat
for use with drinks as well as foods
to provide applications for blind people
to indicate the weight of certain foods

explanation.en: Future uses are drug storage and food weight; freshness, drinks and help for blind people are existing uses.
explanation.kk: Болашақ қолданыстар — дәрі сақтау және тағам салмағы; балғындық, сусындар мен зағиптарға көмек қазірдің өзінде бар.
explanation.ru: Будущие применения — хранение лекарств и вес продуктов; свежесть, напитки и помощь незрячим уже предусмотрены.

items.quote: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that.
items.prompt: Use of local products

explanation.en: Shops should be more proactive about local products, D.
explanation.kk: Дүкендер жергілікті өнімді белсендірек ұсынуы тиіс, D.
explanation.ru: Магазинам следует активнее продвигать местные продукты, D.

items.quote: One thing everyone's aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging — but just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic, The government needs to do something about it.
items.prompt: Reduction in unnecessary packaging

explanation.en: They call for government action, meaning stricter regulation, G.
explanation.kk: Студенттер үкімет әрекетін, яғни қатаңырақ ережені қалайды, G.
explanation.ru: Студенты требуют действий государства, то есть более строгих правил, G.

items.quote: Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now.
items.prompt: Gluten-free and lactose-free food

explanation.en: Many people have bought these foods for years, C; it is already widespread.
explanation.kk: Көп адам мұндай өнімді жылдар бойы сатып алады, C; бұл тек болашақ үрдіс емес.
explanation.ru: Многие уже годами покупают такие продукты, C; это не только будущий тренд.

items.quote: Yeah — I bought a ready-made spice mix for chicken which was supposed to be used by a chef I'd seen on television, and it didn't actually taste of anything.

explanation.kk: Дәмдеуіш қоспасы дәмсіз болды — көңіл қалдыратын нәтиже, B.
explanation.ru: Смесь специй оказалась безвкусной — разочаровывающий результат, B.

items.quote: But people aren't aware of that — it's all kept very quiet.
items.prompt: Development of ‘ghost kitchens’ for takeaway food

explanation.en: People are unaware that the food is made outside the restaurant, F.
explanation.kk: Адамдар тамақ мейрамханадан тыс дайындалатынын білмейді, F.
explanation.ru: Люди не знают, что еда готовится вне ресторана, F.

items.quote: They might be taking a big risk there.
items.prompt: Use of mushrooms for common health concerns

explanation.en: Uncertainty about safe mushroom varieties makes this risky, H.
explanation.kk: Қай саңырауқұлақтың қауіпсіз екені белгісіз; бұл тәуекел, H.
explanation.ru: Неизвестно, какие грибы безопасны; это риск, H.

items.quote: He realised that these must be walls and that they must be thousands of years old for them to predate the bog which subsequently grew over them.
items.prompt: In the 1930s, a local teacher realised that stones beneath the bog surface were once ____.

explanation.en: Caulfield realised the rows of stones were ancient walls, rather than naturally occurring stones.
explanation.kk: Колфилд тас қатарлары табиғи тас емес, көне walls екенін түсінді.
explanation.ru: Колфилд понял, что ряды камней были древними стенами, walls, а не природными камнями.

items.quote: It wasn't until 40 years later, when Patrick Caulfield's son Seamus, who had become an archaeologist by then, began to explore further.
items.prompt: His ____ became an archaeologist and undertook an investigation of the site.

explanation.en: Seamus is identified as Patrick Caulfield’s son and later became an archaeologist.
explanation.kk: Шеймус Патрик Колфилдтің son баласы ретінде аталады және кейін археолог болған.
explanation.ru: Шеймус назван сыном Патрика Колфилда, son, и позднее стал археологом.

items.quote: He inserted iron probes into the bog to map the formation of the stones, a traditional method which local people had always used for finding fuel buried in the bog for thousands of years.
items.prompt: A traditional method used by local people to dig for ____ was used to identify where stones were located.

explanation.en: Iron probes used a local method for finding buried fuel; the question asks what people dug for, not the tool.
explanation.kk: Темір сүңгі көмілген fuel іздеу әдісіне негізделген; сұрақ құралды емес, ізделген затты сұрайды.
explanation.ru: Железные щупы применяли по методу поиска топлива, fuel; спрашивается цель раскопок, а не инструмент.

items.quote: Objects remain so well preserved in these conditions because of the acidity of the peat and the deficiency of oxygen.
items.prompt: Items are well preserved in the bog because of a lack of ____.

explanation.en: Preservation is linked to acidic peat and a deficiency of oxygen; “lack of” means deficiency.
explanation.kk: Сақталу шымтезек қышқылдығы мен oxygen тапшылығына байланысты; lack of — deficiency баламасы.
explanation.ru: Сохранность объясняют кислотностью торфа и недостатком кислорода, oxygen; lack of означает deficiency.

groups.title: Céide Fields — discovery
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: These weren't round as people often assume, but rectangular with a small hole in the roof that allowed smoke to escape.
items.prompt: Houses were ____ in shape and had a hole in the roof.

explanation.en: The houses were rectangular, explicitly contrasted with the common assumption that they were round.
explanation.kk: Үйлер rectangular болған; дөңгелек болған деген болжам тікелей жоққа шығарылады.
explanation.ru: Дома были прямоугольными, rectangular; предположение о круглых домах прямо опровергается.

items.quote: The pots were used for many things; as well as for storing food, pots were filled with a small amount of fat and when this was set alight, they served as lamps.
items.prompt: Neolithic innovations include pots used for storage and to make ____.

explanation.en: Pots containing burning fat served as lamps; storage is the other use already mentioned in the notes.
explanation.kk: Жанып тұрған майы бар құмыралар lamps ретінде қолданылған; сақтау — жазбада берілген басқа қолданыс.
explanation.ru: Горшки с горящим жиром служили лампами, lamps; хранение — другое, уже указанное применение.

items.quote: Evidence from the Céide Fields suggests that each plot of land was of a suitable size to sustain an extended family.
items.prompt: Each field at Céide was large enough to support a big ____.

explanation.en: Each plot could sustain an extended family; the notes paraphrase “extended” as “big”.
explanation.kk: Әр телім үлкен family асырай алған; extended сөзі big арқылы берілген.
explanation.ru: Каждый участок обеспечивал большую семью, family; extended перефразировано словом big.

items.quote: This must have been a year-round activity as no structures have been found which would have been used to shelter animals in the winter.
items.prompt: The fields were probably used to restrict the grazing of animals — no evidence of structures to house them during ____.

explanation.en: No structures were found for sheltering animals in winter; the gap names the season.
explanation.kk: Малды winter кезінде паналататын құрылыс табылмаған; бос орын маусымды сұрайды.
explanation.ru: Не нашли построек для укрытия животных зимой, winter; нужен сезон.

groups.title: Céide Fields — Neolithic farmers
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: The soil would have become less productive and led to the abandonment of farming.
items.prompt: A decline in ____ quality

explanation.en: The soil became less productive; this is the decline in soil quality, not the later rainfall increase.
explanation.kk: Soil құнарлылығы төмендеген; бұл кейінгі жауынның артуы емес, сапаның нашарлауы.
explanation.ru: Почва, soil, стала менее плодородной; это снижение качества, а не последующее увеличение осадков.

items.quote: The farmers at Céide would have enjoyed a relatively dry period, but this began to change and the conditions became wetter as there was a lot more rain.
items.prompt: An increase in ____

explanation.en: The conditions became wetter because there was more rain; this contrasts with the earlier dry period.
explanation.kk: Rain көбейгендіктен жағдай ылғалды болған; бұл бұрынғы құрғақ кезеңге қарама-қарсы.
explanation.ru: Стало влажнее из-за большего количества дождя, rain; это контраст с прежним сухим периодом.

groups.title: Céide Fields — reasons for the decline in farming
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: A presentation describes the discovery and Neolithic farming at Céide Fields.

transcript.text: For my presentation today, I'm going to talk about the Céide Fields in the northwest of Ireland, one of the largest Neolithic sites in the world.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: I recently visited this site and observed the work that is currently being done by a team of archaeologists there.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The site was first discovered in the 1930s by a local teacher, Patrick Caulfield.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: He noticed that when local people were digging in the bog, they were constantly hitting against what seemed to be rows of stones.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: He realised that these must be walls and that they must be thousands of years old for them to predate the bog which subsequently grew over them.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: He wrote to the National Museum in Dublin to ask them to investigate, but no one took him seriously.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It wasn't until 40 years later, when Patrick Caulfield's son Seamus, who had become an archaeologist by then, began to explore further.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: He inserted iron probes into the bog to map the formation of the stones, a traditional method which local people had always used for finding fuel buried in the bog for thousands of years.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Carbon dating later proved that the site was over 5,000 years old and was the largest Neolithic site in Ireland.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Thanks to the bog which covers the area, the remains of the settlement at Céide Fields, which is over 5,000 years old, are extremely well-preserved.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: A bog is 90 percent water; its soil is so saturated that when the grasses and heathers that grow on its surface die, they don't fully decay but accumulate in layers.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Objects remain so well preserved in these conditions because of the acidity of the peat and the deficiency of oxygen.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: At least 175 days of rain a year are required for this to happen; this part of Ireland gets an average of 225 days.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The Neolithic farmers at Céide would have enjoyed several centuries of relative peace and stability.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Neolithic farmers generally lived in larger communities than their predecessors, with a number of houses built around a community building.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: As they lived in permanent settlements, Neolithic farmers were able to build bigger houses.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: These weren't round as people often assume, but rectangular with a small hole in the roof that allowed smoke to escape.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This is one of many innovations and indicates that the Neolithic farmers were the first people to cook indoors.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Another new technology that Neolithic settlers brought to Ireland was pottery.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Fragments of Neolithic pots have been found in Céide and elsewhere in Ireland.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The pots were used for many things; as well as for storing food, pots were filled with a small amount of fat and when this was set alight, they served as lamps.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It's thought that the Céide Fields were mainly used as paddocks for animals to graze in.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Evidence from the Céide Fields suggests that each plot of land was of a suitable size to sustain an extended family.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They may have used a system of rotational grazing in order to prevent over-grazing and to allow for plant recovery and regrowth.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This must have been a year-round activity as no structures have been found which would have been used to shelter animals in the winter.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: However, archaeologists believe that this way of life at Céide ceased abruptly.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Why was this?
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Well, several factors may have contributed to the changing circumstances.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The soil would have become less productive and led to the abandonment of farming.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The crop rotation system was partly responsible for this as it would have been very intensive and was not sustainable.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: But there were also climatic pressures too.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The farmers at Céide would have enjoyed a relatively dry period, but this began to change and the conditions became wetter as there was a lot more rain.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It was these conditions that encouraged the bog to form over the area which survives today.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: So now I'd like to show you some ...
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER
